skill.name: deslop
skill.description: Remove AI-generated code slop from a branch. Use when cleaning up AI-generated code, removing unnecessary comments, defensive checks, or type casts. Checks diff against main and fixes style inconsistencies.

security_audit.summary: The two static findings are false positives caused by Markdown inline code, not executable Ruby or shell backtick execution. The skill is prompt-only and asks the assistant to review a local git diff for code cleanup patterns. No prompt injection, data exfiltration intent, or other semantic security issue was found.

static_findings.snippet: - Casts to `any` to get around type issues
1. Get the diff against main: `git diff main...HEAD`

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 14 uses Markdown inline code around the TypeScript word any. It is not shell syntax, command execution, or user-controlled execution.
Line 20 documents a hardcoded read-only git diff command for local review. The backticks are Markdown formatting and there is no command injection or external data transfer.

content.value_statement: AI-assisted branches often include extra comments, unnecessary defensive code, and weak type workarounds. This skill reviews the branch diff and removes changes that do not match the surrounding code style.
actual_capabilities: Compares the current branch against main using the git diff workflow described by the skill.
Identifies extra comments that do not match nearby human-written code.
Flags unnecessary defensive checks and try/catch blocks in trusted code paths.
Removes avoidable type casts used to bypass type issues.
Moves inline Python imports to the normal import section when needed.
Summarizes cleanup changes in one to three sentences.
limitations: Requires a repository with a meaningful main branch diff.
Depends on the assistant judgment for what counts as inconsistent style.
Does not replace project tests, type checks, or human review.
May need user guidance when defensive code is intentional.

use_cases.title: Review AI-Assisted Pull Requests
use_cases.description: Clean a pull request before review by removing unnatural comments and unnecessary defensive code.

use_cases.title: Prepare Branches For Maintainers
use_cases.description: Make generated changes look consistent with the existing codebase before asking maintainers for feedback.

use_cases.title: Standardize Cleanup Workflows
use_cases.description: Apply a repeatable checklist for removing common AI code artifacts across feature branches.

prompt_templates.title: Clean My Branch
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the deslop skill to review my current branch against main. Remove obvious AI-generated comments, unnecessary defensive checks, and style inconsistencies.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner cleanup before opening a pull request.

prompt_templates.title: Focus On Review Noise
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the deslop skill on this branch. Focus on changes that would distract reviewers, including redundant comments, abnormal try/catch blocks, and avoidable type casts.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate cleanup for a pull request that is close to ready.

prompt_templates.title: Preserve Intentional Safeguards
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the deslop skill, but preserve any defensive checks that protect public inputs or documented edge cases. Summarize each removed pattern briefly.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced cleanup where some safety logic may be intentional.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Generated Refactor
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the deslop skill to review the generated refactor in this branch. Compare each change with nearby style and remove artifacts that do not fit the codebase.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced cleanup after a broad AI-assisted refactor.

output_examples.input: A branch adds several explanatory comments above simple assignments and wraps trusted code in new try/catch blocks.
output_examples.output: Removed redundant comments and unnecessary defensive wrappers while preserving the intended behavior. The branch now matches nearby code style more closely.

output_examples.input: A TypeScript change includes broad type casts to bypass errors in a generated implementation.
output_examples.output: Replaced avoidable type casts with clearer typed values where possible. Left a short note for any remaining type issue that needs follow-up.

output_examples.input: A Python change imports modules inside functions without a local reason.
output_examples.output: Moved inline imports to the top of the file with existing imports. No behavior changes were needed.

best_practices: Run tests and type checks after cleanup to confirm behavior is unchanged.
Preserve defensive checks that protect untrusted input or documented failure modes.
Review the final diff to verify the cleanup matches project conventions.
anti_patterns: Removing comments that explain complex business logic or non-obvious constraints.
Deleting validation from public or security-sensitive code paths without proof.
Treating every type cast as wrong when the surrounding project intentionally uses it.

faq.question: What does this skill clean up?
faq.answer: It removes common AI-generated artifacts such as redundant comments, unusual defensive blocks, weak casts, and inconsistent style.

faq.question: Does it run the project test suite?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on diff review and cleanup. You should run the relevant tests after changes.

faq.question: Can it work without a main branch?
faq.answer: It is designed around comparing the current branch to main. A different base branch may require explicit instructions.

faq.question: Will it remove all defensive code?
faq.answer: No. It should keep checks that protect untrusted input, documented edge cases, or important reliability behavior.

faq.question: Is this useful with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill is prompt-based and is compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: Who should use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it when you want an AI-assisted branch to look consistent before review or merge.
